Draft:

A) A small LRU inside the reader keeps the cache next to the access pattern that benefits from it, so hit-rate tuning and invalidation live in one place. The trade-off: the reader now owns state and lifetime, which makes it harder to test in isolation and easy to leak stale entries across callers who expect a fresh read.

B) A memoized wrapper keeps the reader pure and puts caching policy at the call site, so you can swap or drop it per consumer. The trade-off: every caller has to opt in and agree on the key, and invalidation becomes a coordination problem spread across call sites rather than a single place.

parts.text: I'd write a `memoizeJournalRead(read)` factory that takes the reader function plus a key function, holds a `Map` of key to result, returns the cached value on a hit and calls through to the reader on a miss, and exposes `invalidate(key)` and `clear()` so callers can drop entries explicitly.
